correctness.rationale: For Cr_n=K_n,n minus a perfect matching, each omitted a_i requires a selected b_j adjacent to a_i but to no other omitted A vertex; because b_j is adjacent to all A except a_j, at most two A can be omitted, and symmetrically at most two B. Hence |S|>=2n-4. Equality forces two omitted A indices I={i,j} and two omitted B indices J={k,l}; the unique possible private witnesses b_j,b_i and a_l,a_k must all remain selected, exactly when I∩J=empty. Every such S is super dominating. Its induced subgraph is K_2,2 for n=4; for n>=5, each part has >=3 selected vertices and any missing cross-pair has a selected alternating length-three path, proving connectedness. Counting disjoint index pairs gives binom(n,2)binom(n-2,2). Boundary n=3 is C6 with 15 ordinary vs 6 connected minimum sets. An independent exhaustive definition-based enumerator checks 3<=n<=7.
